contract.sync_assumed: the logical warps of one hardware warp stay converged, the caller separates calls that reuse the output buffer by a __syncwarp on the member mask (the harness does)
contract.sync_performed: 32 / T full-warp redux.sync per round (one per logical warp, the other groups feed the identity), no barriers, no shared memory
contract.n_range: N = T x IPT with T in {4, 8, 16}, measured N 8 to 128
contract.type_constraints: bf16 and fp32 as in W2_packed, int32 indices from the position
contract.tie_break_support: inherent, same code for both requirements (measured at warp scope)

correctness.notes: oracle battery passed on all 46 sub-warp cells, all groups of the launch checked. This batch ran twice on the node 38 seconds apart (..._140035.json and ..._140113.json, same holder), the card uses the second, the two agree within 0.7 percent.

low_level: The masked redux of the baseline compiled to 8 CREDUX inside 5 BSSY, WARPSYNC, BRA, BSYNC regions (one loop per round over the distinct mask values of the warp) in the T 8 N 32 k 4 throughput kernel. The full-warp form has 32 CREDUX (4 per round, one per logical warp with the identity in the other 24 lanes), 17 plain WARPSYNC and 2 BSSY, no loop, 26 registers against 28. At T 4 the kernel has 64 CREDUX for 4 rounds and 20 against 31 registers.

Round cost from the slope over k, bf16 N 32: T 16 (2 groups) 35 cycles against 174, T 8 (4 groups) 34.5 against 327, T 4 (8 groups) 88 against 649. The pipelined redux model of T17 (22 + 6 per extra redux) plus 2 selects per group predicts 34, 46 and 82.

Registers rise by 2 to 10 at k 64 (the G identity selects per round), occupancy drops from 8 to 6 at T 8 N 32 k 16 and from 6 to 4 at T 8 N 128 k 64, fp32 T 4 N 128 k 16 and 64 stay at 168 to 228 registers (IPT 32 fp32 with the v1 tie pass) at occupancy 1. No spills except the 76 bytes both forms have at fp32 T 4 N 128 k 16. Canary 32.001 at start and end, R squared 1.0000, node umbriel-b200-047.
algorithmic: Latency gains of 2.2x to 7.1x over the masked baseline in every cell: bf16 T 8 N 32 k 4 295 against 1433 (4.9x), T 8 N 128 k 8 (gpt-oss and Qwen3 routers) 802 against 3152 (3.9x), T 16 N 128 k 16 782 against 3162 (4.0x), T 4 N 8 k 4 369 against 2636 (7.1x), fp32 T 8 N 32 k 4 512 against 1965 (3.8x). The sub-warp primitive now costs about the warp primitive at the same N and k plus 6 cycles per extra group per round: T 16 N 32 k 4 196 against 124 at warp scope.

Throughput gains are 1.1x to 1.7x (bf16 T 8 N 8 k 4 239 against 139 Gelem/s, T 8 N 128 k 8 775 against 670) because the masked form's serialized passes already overlapped across the 8 warps of a block, fp32 T 4 N 128 k 16 and 64 gain 2.1 to 2.3x where the baseline was at occupancy 1 with a long serialized chain.
Rows per hardware warp trade latency for throughput as the card expected: at N 128 k 8 bf16, T 16 (2 rows) 474 cycles and 717 Gelem/s, T 8 (4 rows) 802 and 775, T 4 (8 rows) 1647 and 760.
negative: At 8 groups per warp (T 4) the round costs 88 cycles, 3.5x the warp round, so T 4 is only for N 8 rows (the Mixtral and DBRX shapes) where the prologue is one sort of 2 items.
The identity selects cost registers at k 64 (T 8 N 128 k 64: 79 against 72) and one occupancy step in two cells.
surprises: The compiler emits WARPSYNC before full-mask collectives inside the logical-warp code (17 of them) even though the warp is converged, at no measurable cost, while the masked form's WARPSYNC loop costs 60 to 80 cycles per group per round.
open_questions: A 2-step shuffle tree at T 4 (about 60 cycles) against the 8-redux form (88), and whether match-free ballot tricks (one full-warp ballot of head equality after the group max) could emit the winner without the per-group select.
The fp32 cells here still run the v1 counting tie pass (policy_sw_v2 keeps it), sw_v3 with the next-word check and odd-even blocks is built and not measured.
